title: Single-neuron position/direction encoding
current_best_explanation: No current global winner has been verified on this exact frozen input, split and scorer. A published dataset name or broad leaderboard lead is insufficient.
executed_endpoint: One rat hippocampal teaching recording; position in cm and velocity in cm/s every 20 ms, chronological 60/40 split with one-second buffer. Predict 20-ms spike counts. Bits per spike against training-mean rate; no test spike history, population recordings or stimulus video supplied.

existing_reference.name: Fixed quadratic position × movement-direction Poisson GLM with tiny L2
existing_reference.evidence: A: exact local supervised encoding reference.
existing_reference.strength: Correct observation model and a valid simple place-field basis.
problems: A quadratic basis can severely underfit place-field geometry.
One cell/session is not a neural population encoding benchmark.
Fixed tiny regularization was not broad training-only model selection.
existing_reference.verification_scope: Only the named locally audited reference/archived outputs, not every newer candidate or equal-budget/global optimality.

candidates.name: NeMoS spline/tensor-product Poisson GLM
candidates.evidence: B: maintained domain software; exact frozen-slice result absent.
candidates.information_match: Direct position/direction/count input match; tune basis complexity and regularization on contiguous training blocks.

candidates.name: Poisson generalized additive model with direction interaction
candidates.information_match: Same available covariates, nonnegative rates, training-only smoothness selection; velocity magnitude can be used without adding measurements.

candidates.name: Spike-history / population latent neural models
candidates.evidence: B as broad software capability, D for input match.
candidates.information_match: Need withheld spike histories, simultaneous units or richer stimuli; not valid replacements under L04.

recommended_next_comparator: Train-block-selected spline position × direction Poisson GLM/GAM implemented in NeMoS or equivalent numerical code, with a small predeclared penalty/basis grid.
switching_assessment: UPGRADE the flexible conventional encoding reference, high priority, Tier B/C. Preserve original quadratic GLM. A modern population foundation model would change the observation/information regime; no current universal place-cell winner is identified.
limitations: Chronological drift and buffer influence apparent generalization.
Only one rat/cell/session: no biological-population confidence or cross-animal claim.
Training CV must be contiguous with a buffer, not shuffled 20-ms bins.
No test count conditioning or recurrent update with scored targets.
NeMoS is a toolkit; choosing it does not itself certify optimal basis or fitting.
The live tutorial displays a nonconvergence warning in its example; comparator implementation must check convergence rather than copy settings blindly.
